title: A Perfectly Preserved Library
text: Shelves to the ceiling, every book dry and whole, a reading lamp still burning on the desk beside an open page. The ink on it is wet. Nothing this far down should be this well kept, and nobody this far down should be reading.

options.label: The sharpest mind sits down at the open page, unable to resist what was left there for them.

outcomes.text: Hours pass like minutes. They come up with pages of notes and a headache that will last a week.
Some of what they read keeps reading them back, long after the book is closed.
They read a recipe for something, and now they are always hungry for it. They do not say what it calls for.

options.label: Burn it, every book. Whoever reads down here does not deserve a library.

outcomes.text: The books burn slowly, page by curling page, and something in the stacks screams once, and then is silent.

options.label: The lightest-laden carries one book out, the one that seems to want to leave.

outcomes.text: The book is heavier than it looks, and warm, and worth it. It does not like the light.
